title: Triples That Sum to Zero
statement:
Given an array of integers nums, find every group of three values, taken from three different positions, that adds up to 0.

Return each group once. Two groups are the same if they hold the same three values, no matter which positions they came from. A value may appear twice or three times in a group if it appears that often in nums.

Any order is accepted: the groups can come in any order, and the values inside a group can too. Return an empty list if there is no such group.

examples.why: There are two -1s, so [-1, 0, 1] can be built from two different position sets. It is still listed once.
Four ways to pick three zeros, one group of values.
The value 2 is used twice because it appears at two positions. Deduplicating the input first would lose this group.

hints: Fix the first value of the triple. What problem is left for the other two?
With the first value fixed at a, you need two values that sum to −a. If the array were sorted, you already know an O(n) way to find such pairs.

Sort once. For each i, run two pointers on the part to its right. Skip a value equal to the previous one at the same role (first value, and the left pointer after a hit) so each group is produced once.

explain.intuition:
Sorting turns this into n copies of a problem you know. Fix the smallest value of the triple at position i; the other two must sum to −nums[i] and lie to the right of i. On a sorted slice, two pointers find all such pairs in one sweep.

Sorting also makes duplicates easy. Equal values sit next to each other, so if nums[i] equals nums[i − 1], every triple it could start was already found. After a hit, move the left pointer past all copies of its value for the same reason. Nothing needs a set.
steps: Sort a copy of the array numerically.
For each i: if nums[i] > 0, stop, since three positive values cannot sum to 0. If nums[i] equals the previous value, skip it.
Set lo = i + 1 and hi = n − 1. While lo < hi, compare nums[i] + nums[lo] + nums[hi] with 0: below 0 move lo right, above 0 move hi left.
On a hit, record the triple, move both pointers inward, and keep moving lo while it lands on the same value as before.
pitfalls: Calling sort() without a comparator in JavaScript. It sorts as strings, so [10, -8, 3] becomes [-8, 10, 3] and the two-pointer logic breaks. Use (a, b) => a − b.
Removing duplicates from the input first: [2, -4, 2, 1] needs both 2s.
Skipping duplicates of nums[i] by comparing with nums[i + 1] instead of nums[i − 1]. That skips the first copy, and with it the triples that use two copies, like [-1, -1, 2].

complexity.space: O(1) besides the sorted copy and the output

solutions.title: Every triple, deduplicated with a set
solutions.idea: Three nested loops. Sort each hit and use its text form as a key to skip groups already seen.

solutions.title: Sort, then two pointers for each first value
solutions.idea: Fix the first value, find the other two with two pointers on the sorted rest, and skip equal neighbours to avoid repeats.

followups: Find the triple whose sum is closest to a given target.
Generalise to groups of four values that sum to a target. What is the complexity, and where do the duplicate checks go?
